Summary: Assess new third-party components through identity, license, provenance, security, SBOM, and approval steps so reuse remains deliberate and auditable.
ValueStatement: Make open-source adoption safe, fast, and reusable by standardizing component intake, license obligation review, provenance checks, and durable approval records.
InterfaceContractSummary: A requested component or package becomes an approved or rejected intake decision with explicit obligations, provenance evidence, and SBOM updates.
GovernanceNotes: Do not confuse convenient package acquisition with approved component adoption. Identity, obligations, provenance, and update ownership must be explicit.
ChangeSummary: Built from OpenChain resources, SPDX metadata practice, SLSA provenance expectations, and SSDF supply-chain protections.
GovernancePolicySummary: No component may be adopted without verified identity, license review, security/provenance assessment, SBOM registration, and accountable ongoing ownership.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: A component can be popular and still be unsuitable; approval requires explicit reasoning, not reputation transfer.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with human legal/security approval. Automation may collect evidence and draft analysis, but approval remains accountable.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Works for procurement-style intake, dev-team self-service review, and AI-assisted package research pipelines.
Metrics: Percentage of adopted components with current SBOM entry
Number of approvals with unresolved provenance gaps
Time to publish obligation guidance to consuming teams
Risks: Component identity is wrong or incomplete.
License obligations are misunderstood or not passed downstream.
Provenance or build integrity is weak relative to sensitivity of use.
SBOM updates lag behind real adoption.
TailoringRules: For internal low-risk tooling, security review may be lighter but SBOM and ownership still remain required.
For runtime production dependencies, provenance and maintenance posture must be stricter.
For AI/ML model packages and datasets, add the AI evaluation and dataset handling sidecars.

Steps.Title: Register component intake request
Steps.Subtitle: Make the request explicit before evaluation
Steps.Notes: Capture why the component is wanted, where it will be used, what alternatives exist, and who will own it after approval.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Package name or component identifier, intended use, business context, and requesting team.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Typed component intake request with accountable owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Software engineer requests; service owner confirms operational ownership exists.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject anonymous or ownerless component requests.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Requester remains accountable for supplying context.

Steps.Title: Verify component identity and maintenance posture
Steps.Subtitle: Know exactly what you are evaluating
Steps.Notes: Confirm upstream source, package lineage, maintainer activity, release freshness, and whether the requested artifact matches the claimed project.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Component request, repository links, package registry metadata, and maintainer signals.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Verified identity record and maintenance posture summary.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Identity note, upstream mapping, and maintenance-health summary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: SBOM curator verifies identity; software engineer helps interpret practical adoption implications.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not continue if the requested package cannot be reliably tied to an upstream project and maintenance history.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Identity verification remains with the catalog steward.

Steps.Title: Analyze license obligations and redistribution constraints
Steps.Subtitle: Adoption must preserve downstream compliance
Steps.Notes: Translate the component license, notice requirements, source obligations, export constraints, and policy exceptions into explicit obligations.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Verified identity, license texts, notice files, policy guidance, and intended distribution model.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Obligation matrix and legal position for adoption.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: License-obligation matrix and unresolved legal questions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: License counsel owns legal interpretation; compliance steward reviews policy fit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No approval if obligations cannot be explained to downstream teams.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Legal interpretation remains with qualified counsel.

Steps.Title: Review security posture and provenance trust
Steps.Subtitle: Supply-chain trust must match deployment risk
Steps.Notes: Assess known vulnerabilities, update responsiveness, maintainer trust, signed provenance, and build-chain confidence relative to intended use.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Identity record, license position, vulnerability data, provenance statements, and deployment context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Supply-chain risk position with compensating controls or rejection rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security/provenance review note and risk position.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer may reject a component even if the license is acceptable.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not approve runtime-critical components on weak provenance without explicit compensating controls.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security and provenance review remain explicit.

Steps.Title: Approve, reject, or constrain adoption
Steps.Subtitle: Approval carries obligations forward
Steps.Notes: Make the adoption decision and publish the resulting obligations, owner, approved version boundary, and review cadence.
Steps.InputContractSummary: License position, security/provenance review, and intended use context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approval decision with obligations, owner, and review cadence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval record and final SBOM registration.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Compliance steward approves policy fit; service owner accepts operational ownership.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No approval without named ongoing owner and explicit version boundary.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Approved
BranchOutcomes.Description: Component may be adopted under recorded conditions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Rejected
BranchOutcomes.Description: Component is not approved for the intended use.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Legal review is retained in the record.

Steps.Title: Hand off obligations and establish re-review triggers
Steps.Subtitle: Approval must become operational practice
Steps.Notes: Publish obligation guidance, notify consuming teams, and define the triggers that force re-review when component posture changes.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approval record, SBOM entry, obligations matrix, and owner contacts.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Downstream handoff package and re-review trigger list.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Obligation handoff note and re-review log.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: SBOM curator owns metadata dissemination; service owner owns runtime review cadence.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If obligations cannot be passed to consuming teams, the adoption is not operationally complete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Catalog dissemination remains with the SBOM curator.

LocalRoles.Summary: Specialist reviewer for open-source license obligations, incompatibilities, and exception framing.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Ensure component use decisions reflect actual license obligations and approved exception logic.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A legal or licensing specialist focused on OSS usage governance.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Specialist reviewer for open-source license obligations, incompatibilities, and exception framing.
KnowledgeRequirements: Deep knowledge of common open-source licenses, notice obligations, reciprocity triggers, and distribution models.
Ability to interpret license implications in the actual product delivery context.
Knowledge of when engineering or product assumptions create legal risk.
Understanding of exception and approval patterns for non-standard component use.
Ability to separate opinion, precedent, and mandatory restriction clearly.
Knowledge of how license obligations interact with third-party distribution and customer commitments.
ExperienceRequirements: Has reviewed OSS component usage for a commercial product or enterprise environment.
Has handled license incompatibility or obligation-escalation scenarios.
Has written or approved a licensing position that guided engineering action.
Has worked with compliance stewards and engineers on OSS policy execution.
Has helped define reusable policy patterns for repeated component intake.
DecisionRights: Approve, reject, or conditionally approve license acceptability.
Require notices, attribution, or exception handling before component adoption.
Escalate unresolved incompatibility to accountable governance owners.
Define whether a component can move forward with conditions.
CollaborationExpectations: Work with compliance steward, SBOM curator, and engineers.
Review policy questions early enough to avoid wasted implementation effort.
Document precedent carefully for future reuse.
AntiPatterns: Treating popular components as automatically safe from a license standpoint.
Giving vague legal caution without a usable recommendation.
Approving exceptions without required follow-up obligations.
Waiting until release to ask how the component is actually distributed.
FitnessEvidence: Clear licensing decisions consumed by delivery teams.
Documented obligation patterns reused across component reviews.
Audit or legal review confidence in the role’s output.

LocalRoles.Summary: Metadata owner for component inventory, provenance completeness, and reusable dependency evidence.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Keep the software bill of materials and dependency evidence accurate enough for governance, response, and later reuse.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A supply-chain operations specialist who can structure component metadata and evidence consistently.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Metadata owner for component inventory, provenance completeness, and reusable dependency evidence.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior release engineering or supply-chain operations
KnowledgeRequirements: Knowledge of SBOM concepts, provenance metadata, component identifiers, and dependency relationship modeling.
Ability to collect and normalize component data from build, package, and repository sources.
Understanding of how missing metadata weakens vulnerability and compliance response.
Knowledge of SPDX-compatible or equivalent metadata structures and reuse expectations.
Ability to track completeness, gaps, and manual overrides transparently.
Understanding of retention and sensitivity requirements for supply-chain evidence.
ExperienceRequirements: Has built or maintained component inventory or SBOM outputs for a software product.
Has reconciled incomplete dependency metadata and documented the gaps.
Has worked with engineering, security, and compliance on dependency evidence needs.
Has supported vulnerability-response or audit work using component metadata.
Has improved repeatability of dependency evidence generation.
DecisionRights: Approve metadata completeness for the OSS intake gate.
Require missing provenance or component identifiers before release use.
Escalate when dependency evidence is not reproducible.
Define reuse restrictions for incomplete or provisional SBOM outputs.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate with platform, security, and license roles.
Keep evidence structured, versioned, and reviewable.
Document manual assumptions instead of burying them.
Support rapid lookup during vulnerability or audit events.
AntiPatterns: Publishing an SBOM that looks complete but contains unexplained blind spots.
Treating dependency metadata as a one-time release artifact instead of a reusable capability.
Ignoring transitive or generated dependencies that materially affect risk.
FitnessEvidence: Structured SBOM outputs used in later reviews or incidents.
Traceable reconciliation notes for incomplete metadata.
Stakeholder trust in the curator’s completeness signals.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Matrix of component-specific obligations, notices, approvals, and residual restrictions for the intake decision.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release packaging, audit response, and future version updates of the same component family.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify which obligation applies to which component and usage mode.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Ensures the team knows exactly what component is being approved and from where.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: A new component or version has been proposed.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Identity, source, and version are explicit enough for reproducible review and later response.
Checks: Component name, version, and upstream source are captured.
Build or package identity is linked where available.
Transitive risk blind spots are called out.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms all relevant license obligations were identified and assigned.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Component obligations are explicit and mapped to a concrete delivery or compliance action where needed.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: License interpretation remains ambiguous or obligations have no owner.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate to compliance steward and sponsoring manager before component approval.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for the final component approval summary.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to state unrestricted approval while major provenance or obligation gaps remain.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Produce working change artifacts that satisfy the process contract, surface blockers quickly, and leave enough proof for review and reuse.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A build-capable engineer who can turn scope into code, tests, documentation, and traceable technical decisions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Implementation owner for code, automated tests, and change-level technical evidence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Represent live-service constraints, operational history, and post-release accountability in change decisions.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A domain-aligned owner with authority over service-level objectives, support load, and operational trade-offs.
RoleUsages.Notes: Operational accountability owner for a live service, product surface, or bounded business capability.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Keep the software bill of materials and dependency evidence accurate enough for governance, response, and later reuse.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A supply-chain operations specialist who can structure component metadata and evidence consistently.
RoleUsages.Notes: Metadata owner for component inventory, provenance completeness, and reusable dependency evidence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Ensure component use decisions reflect actual license obligations and approved exception logic.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A legal or licensing specialist focused on OSS usage governance.
RoleUsages.Notes: Specialist reviewer for open-source license obligations, incompatibilities, and exception framing.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Ensure required compliance considerations are identified early, translated into actionable checks, and retained as evidence.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A governance specialist who understands how policy obligations intersect with real delivery work.
RoleUsages.Notes: Policy and evidence steward for contractual, regulatory, license, and audit-sensitive change decisions.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Ensure changes touching trust boundaries, sensitive data, dependencies, or operational attack surface are reviewed proportionally and documented defensibly.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior security practitioner who can translate security risk into concrete engineering and governance decisions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Security gate owner for threat assessment, exception handling, and trust-boundary decisions.
